scenes.tts: The energy pyramid followed only the tissue branch. What happens to energy that never becomes tissue for the next level? Return to the same Bay. Gold energy and green carbon now travel together, then separate.
scenes.caption: The energy pyramid followed only the tissue branch. What happens to energy that never becomes tissue for the next level? Return to the same Bay. Gold energy and green carbon now travel together, then separate.
scenes.visual: Hook first in the same Chesapeake Bay cross-section and exact COLOR MAP from the first film: energy GOLD, living carbon and producer tissue GREEN, consumers TEAL, decomposers BLUE, heat RED. Send paired GOLD and GREEN pulses from phytoplankton toward a menhaden. At the menhaden, split them toward two large question marks. Keep water, plankton, and fish moving. No title yet.
scenes.narration: The energy pyramid followed only the tissue branch. What happens to energy that never becomes tissue for the next level? Return to the same Bay. Gold energy and green carbon now travel together, then separate.

scenes.visual: Keep the Bay moving behind a two-second title, 'Energy Flows, Matter Returns'. Transform the title into two small corner trackers: a straight GOLD arrow and a GREEN loop.

scenes.tts: Sunlight enters the Bay as radiant energy. Phytoplankton change some into chemical energy in food. Consumers change food energy into movement, new tissue, and red heat. Energy is never made or destroyed. It changes form as organisms live.
scenes.caption: Sunlight enters the Bay as radiant energy. Phytoplankton change some into chemical energy in food. Consumers change food energy into movement, new tissue, and red heat. Energy is never made or destroyed. It changes form as organisms live.
scenes.visual: A GOLD pulse falls from the sun and fills GREEN phytoplankton. Transform the same pulse into a GOLD food band entering TEAL zooplankton, then menhaden. At each, branch the band into moving fins, a growing tissue patch, and expanding RED heat waves. Keep the straight GOLD tracker advancing.
scenes.narration: Sunlight enters the Bay as radiant energy. Phytoplankton change some into chemical energy in food. Consumers change food energy into movement, new tissue, and red heat. Energy is never made or destroyed. It changes form as organisms live.

scenes.tts: Heat spreads through water and air. No living thing can capture that dispersed heat to build food again. The gold path moves forward and fades outward as red ripples. Nearly every ecosystem needs a continuing energy supply. In the Bay, that supply is sunlight.
scenes.caption: Heat spreads through water and air. No living thing can capture that dispersed heat to build food again. The gold path moves forward and fades outward as red ripples. Nearly every ecosystem needs a continuing energy supply. In the Bay, that supply is sunlight.
scenes.visual: Zoom out. RED ripples spread across the water and upward into air while their opacity falls. Try to bend one faded ripple back toward phytoplankton, then let it continue outward instead. A new GOLD pulse arrives from the sun. Label the outgoing ripples 'dispersed heat' and the incoming path 'new energy supply'.
scenes.narration: Heat spreads through water and air. No living thing can capture that dispersed heat to build food again. The gold path moves forward and fades outward as red ripples. Nearly every ecosystem needs a continuing energy supply. In the Bay, that supply is sunlight.

scenes.tts: A menhaden dies, and blue decomposers break it down. Can they return both its carbon and its usable food energy to phytoplankton? Hold both paths in mind.
scenes.caption: A menhaden dies, and blue decomposers break it down. Can they return both its carbon and its usable food energy to phytoplankton? Hold both paths in mind.
scenes.visual: Let one menhaden settle to the bottom as BLUE decomposers gather. Place a GREEN carbon token and a GOLD energy token inside it. Draw two dotted possible return paths toward phytoplankton, each ending in a question mark. Keep decomposers pulsing and water drifting.
scenes.narration: A menhaden dies, and blue decomposers break it down. Can they return both its carbon and its usable food energy to phytoplankton? Hold both paths in mind.

scenes.visual: Deliberate thinking pause. Keep both dotted return paths and the question visible for 4.5 seconds. The GREEN and GOLD tokens pulse alternately. Do not reveal either path.

scenes.tts: Decomposers release much of the menhaden's green carbon as carbon dioxide. Phytoplankton can take that carbon up again. The green path closes into a loop. Energy does not. Decomposers also respire, so more chemical energy becomes heat and leaves the usable food pathway.
scenes.caption: Decomposers release much of the menhaden's green carbon as carbon dioxide. Phytoplankton can take that carbon up again. The green path closes into a loop. Energy does not. Decomposers also respire, so more chemical energy becomes heat and leaves the usable food pathway.
scenes.visual: Reveal the GREEN token as 'carbon dioxide'; move it through water into phytoplankton and close the GREEN loop. Break the GOLD dotted return path to phytoplankton. Split the GOLD token at the BLUE decomposers: one part fills new decomposer tissue, labeled 'decomposer growth', and the respired part transforms into expanding RED heat waves. Neither branch returns usable energy to phytoplankton. Keep the straight GOLD tracker pointing outward.
scenes.narration: Decomposers release much of the menhaden's green carbon as carbon dioxide. Phytoplankton can take that carbon up again. The green path closes into a loop. Energy does not. Decomposers also respire, so more chemical energy becomes heat and leaves the usable food pathway.

scenes.tts: Compare the maps. Carbon atoms pass through organisms, air, and water, and can be reused. Some may be buried or carried away. Energy enters, changes form, and disperses as heat. Matter mostly cycles. Energy moves forward through this sunlit ecosystem.
scenes.caption: Compare the maps. Carbon atoms pass through organisms, air, and water, and can be reused. Some may be buried or carried away. Energy enters, changes form, and disperses as heat. Matter mostly cycles. Energy moves forward through this sunlit ecosystem.
scenes.visual: Place the GREEN loop and straight GOLD-to-RED path side by side over the same Bay, not on separate slides. Animate GREEN tokens circling and let a few peel off toward labels 'buried' and 'carried away'. Animate fresh GOLD entering while RED leaves. Label both diagrams 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Compare the maps. Carbon atoms pass through organisms, air, and water, and can be reused. Some may be buried or carried away. Energy enters, changes form, and disperses as heat. Matter mostly cycles. Energy moves forward through this sunlit ecosystem.

scenes.tts: Not every ecosystem starts with sunlight. Some deep-sea vent communities begin with chemical energy. That changes the entrance, but energy still disperses as heat. The Bay picture has a clear scope, not a universal starting source.
scenes.caption: Not every ecosystem starts with sunlight. Some deep-sea vent communities begin with chemical energy. That changes the entrance, but energy still disperses as heat. The Bay picture has a clear scope, not a universal starting source.
scenes.visual: Keep the GOLD straight-path tracker. Briefly transform the Bay's sun entrance into a labeled block 'chemical energy at a deep-sea vent'; do not draw molecules. The middle transformations and RED heat exit remain in place. Then return to the Bay and add a small scope label, 'sunlit ecosystem'.
scenes.narration: Not every ecosystem starts with sunlight. Some deep-sea vent communities begin with chemical energy. That changes the entrance, but energy still disperses as heat. The Bay picture has a clear scope, not a universal starting source.

scenes.tts: Ecologists test the picture with energy budgets. They compare neighboring feeding levels using matching measurements over the same area and time. Intake, new tissue production, and standing biomass are different measures. Mixing them makes a false transfer percentage.
scenes.caption: Ecologists test the picture with energy budgets. They compare neighboring feeding levels using matching measurements over the same area and time. Intake, new tissue production, and standing biomass are different measures. Mixing them makes a false transfer percentage.
scenes.visual: Transform the Bay into two large adjacent level bars while leaving the GREEN loop and GOLD path as corner trackers. Three ruler frames slide over the bars: 'intake', 'new tissue per year', and 'biomass now'. Only matching ruler frames click together. A mismatched pair stays apart under the warning 'do not divide'. No arithmetic appears.
scenes.narration: Ecologists test the picture with energy budgets. They compare neighboring feeding levels using matching measurements over the same area and time. Intake, new tissue production, and standing biomass are different measures. Mixing them makes a false transfer percentage.

scenes.tts: Transfer percentages vary among ecosystems and feeding steps. Temperature, what gets eaten, digestion, and respiration can change the share reaching new tissue. That variation does not turn energy into a cycle. It changes how wide the next gold band becomes before the remaining energy disperses.
scenes.caption: Transfer percentages vary among ecosystems and feeding steps. Temperature, what gets eaten, digestion, and respiration can change the share reaching new tissue. That variation does not turn energy into a cycle. It changes how wide the next gold band becomes before the remaining energy disperses.
scenes.visual: Return the comparison bars to the Bay. Move a simple condition slider labeled 'conditions' without numbers. The next GOLD tissue band widens and narrows schematically while RED heat and decomposer-bound branches change with it. Keep the GOLD path straight and the GREEN carbon loop cycling throughout.
scenes.narration: Transfer percentages vary among ecosystems and feeding steps. Temperature, what gets eaten, digestion, and respiration can change the share reaching new tissue. That variation does not turn energy into a cycle. It changes how wide the next gold band becomes before the remaining energy disperses.

scenes.tts: Return to the osprey's fish. Its carbon may later enter decomposers, carbon dioxide, and phytoplankton again. Its energy can power movement or growth only before becoming dispersed heat. The same organism belongs to a matter loop and a forward energy path.
scenes.caption: Return to the osprey's fish. Its carbon may later enter decomposers, carbon dioxide, and phytoplankton again. Its energy can power movement or growth only before becoming dispersed heat. The same organism belongs to a matter loop and a forward energy path.
scenes.visual: Center one moving menhaden. Send GREEN carbon from it around the full decomposer-to-carbon-dioxide-to-phytoplankton loop. At the same time, send GOLD energy through movement and tissue, then outward as RED heat. Keep both routes visible and separate.
scenes.narration: Return to the osprey's fish. Its carbon may later enter decomposers, carbon dioxide, and phytoplankton again. Its energy can power movement or growth only before becoming dispersed heat. The same organism belongs to a matter loop and a forward energy path.

scenes.tts: Keep paths separate when reading any food web. Energy flows through ecosystems, while matter cycles and can be reused.
scenes.caption: Keep paths separate when reading any food web. Energy flows through ecosystems, while matter cycles and can be reused.
scenes.visual: Let the Bay fade while the straight GOLD path and GREEN loop enlarge to fill the frame. Move one last GOLD pulse outward and one GREEN token around the loop, then prepare the end card.
scenes.narration: Keep paths separate when reading any food web. Energy flows through ecosystems, while matter cycles and can be reused.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only, centered large: 'Energy flows through ecosystems, while matter cycles and can be reused.' No subtitle, logo line, or smaller text. A faint GOLD arrow moves right as a faint GREEN loop turns behind the words.
